issues.legal_issue: A court may consider an application to add an accused on the basis of a witness’s examination-in-chief before cross-examination is complete.
material_facts: An application to add a person as an accused was made after a witness’s examination-in-chief implicated him but before that witness’s cross-examination was complete.
The Court considered conflicting two-judge decisions on whether cross-examination must be complete before the power is exercised.
The Court noted that a person added as an accused is protected by a fresh commencement of proceedings and the rehearing of witnesses.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that an application may be considered before cross-examination is complete, because the examination-in-chief is evidence and cross-examination follows the person’s addition as an accused. In light of conflicting decisions, it referred the question to a three-judge Bench for consideration.
issues.legal_principle: Section 319(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure uses “evidence” in a broad sense, and Section 319(4) provides for fresh proceedings and rehearing of witnesses against a person added as an accused. Rakesh v. State of Haryana held that recorded testimony may support exercise of the power before cross-examination; Mohd. Shafi v. Mohd. Rafiq held otherwise. The Court also relied on the principle in Nagavva v. Veeranna that a person has no right to be heard before process is issued, and on State of H.P. v. Surinder Mohan concerning the time at which a right to cross-examine arises.

predicates.criminal_trial_seeking_additional_accuse: The proceeding is a criminal trial in which a person not already accused is sought to be added.
predicates.witness_examination_in_chief_implicates_: A witness gives examination-in-chief testimony implicating a person who is not already an accused.

issues.definition: When a person is sought to be added as an accused in a criminal trial and examination-in-chief implicates that person, the testimony may be considered without waiting for cross-examination to be complete.

issues.legal_issue: The threshold for exercising the power to add an accused, including whether conviction must appear likely, required reconsideration because of conflicting decisions.
material_facts: The person sought to be added had been named in the first information report, arrested at the scene with a weapon, and implicated in trial testimony.
The investigating agency later excluded him from the charge-sheet, and an application was made during trial to add him as an accused.
A prior decision had stated that the court must be satisfied that the person would in all likelihood be convicted.
The Court considered that this test substantially curtailed the discretion conferred by the statutory provision and referred the question for reconsideration.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the likelihood-of-conviction test stated in Mohd. Shafi was not in consonance with the statutory provision and required fresh consideration. It referred the question of the proper test and guidelines to a three-judge Bench without finally settling the applicable threshold.
issues.legal_principle: Section 319(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure requires that it appear from the evidence that a person not already accused committed an offence for which that person could be tried with the accused. Joginder Singh v. State of Punjab and Michael Machado v. Central Bureau of Investigation describe the requirement in terms of sufficient evidence or reasonable satisfaction; Ram Kishan Rohtagi v. Municipal Corporation of Delhi and Krishnappa v. State of Karnataka describe the power as extraordinary and to be exercised sparingly for compelling reasons. The Court considered the additional likelihood-of-conviction formulation in Mohd. Shafi inconsistent with the statutory text and referred the question for reconsideration.

predicates.criminal_trial_seeking_additional_accuse: The proceeding is a criminal trial in which a person not already accused is sought to be added.
predicates.conflicting_prior_decisions_on_summoning: Earlier decisions state conflicting standards for the evidence or satisfaction needed to add a person as an accused.

issues.definition: When a criminal trial seeking an additional accused presents conflicting prior standards for summoning, the question of the proper threshold is referred for consideration by a larger bench.

issues.legal_issue: An investigating officer’s completion report must report the prescribed investigative information and must not make judicial findings or grant a person a clean chit.
material_facts: After investigation, a senior police officer submitted a report recommending that two persons not be proceeded against.
The report declared that the persons were innocent and made findings about whether they were present during the incident.
The Court found that the report went beyond reporting the investigation and purported to exercise a court’s function.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the report was not in accordance with law insofar as it made findings and gave a clean chit; deciding whether to act on the report is for the Magistrate under the Code.
issues.legal_principle: Section 173(1) and (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure requires investigation to be completed without unnecessary delay and a report to be forwarded to the Magistrate containing the prescribed information, including whether an offence appears to have been committed and by whom. The investigating officer reports the investigation and does not exercise the judicial power of the Magistrate to determine the matter.

predicates.criminal_investigation_completion_report: A police officer submits a report after completing an investigation into an alleged offence.
predicates.officer_makes_adjudicative_findings_or_g: The officer declares a person innocent or makes a conclusive finding about guilt or involvement rather than reporting investigative information.

issues.definition: A completion report exceeds the officer’s role when, in an investigation, it makes an adjudicative finding or grants a person a clean chit.

issues.legal_issue: The refusal to add a person as an accused did not warrant interference where the Court found no material against him and the lower courts had accepted the investigative report.
material_facts: An application was made during trial to add a person as an accused after a witness was said to have identified him as a member of the unlawful assembly.
The police had reported that he was innocent, and the trial court and High Court accepted that report.
The Supreme Court stated that there was nothing against the person and found no infirmity in the lower courts’ decisions.
issues.conclusion: The Court found no infirmity in the refusal to add the person as an accused and did not interfere with the lower courts’ orders.
issues.legal_principle: Section 319(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure permits a court to proceed against a person when the evidence indicates that the person committed an offence triable with the existing accused. The Court applied the principle that the power is discretionary and that the record must provide a basis for proceeding; it also considered the lower courts’ acceptance of the investigative report.

predicates.appeal_challenges_refusal_to_add_accused: An appeal challenges a lower court’s refusal to add a person as an accused during a criminal trial.
predicates.court_finds_no_material_against_person: The Court finds no material in the record against the person sought to be added.
predicates.lower_courts_accepted_investigative_repo: The trial court and the reviewing court accepted the investigative report concerning the person.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges refusal to add an accused, the Court finds no material against that person, and the lower courts accepted the investigative report, the refusal is not disturbed.

issues.legal_issue: The refusal to add a person as an accused did not warrant interference where the lower courts had considered the investigative report and their decision was not unlawful or unwarranted.
material_facts: A person who had not been charge-sheeted was identified in trial testimony as having been present and participated in the incident.
The investigating agency’s report stated that he was not present, and the trial court and High Court considered that report when refusing to issue process.
The Supreme Court concluded that the lower courts’ order could not be termed unlawful or unwarranted.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere with the refusal to issue process against the person.
issues.legal_principle: Section 319(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure permits a court to proceed against a person who appears from the evidence to have committed an offence triable with the accused. The Court considered the investigative report and the lower courts’ assessment in deciding whether their refusal to issue process required interference.

predicates.appeal_challenges_refusal_to_issue_proce: An appeal challenges a lower court’s refusal to issue process against a person during a criminal trial.
predicates.person_was_not_charge_sheeted: The investigating agency did not include the person in the charge-sheet.
predicates.lower_courts_considered_investigative_re: The lower courts considered the investigating agency’s report when deciding whether to issue process.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges refusal to issue process against a person not charge-sheeted and the lower courts considered the investigative report, the refusal is not disturbed if the Court finds no basis to interfere.

issues.legal_issue: The evidence concerning a person named in the first information report, arrested at the scene with a weapon, and implicated in trial testimony prima facie supported adding him as an accused.
material_facts: The person’s name appeared in the first information report.
Police arrested him at the scene, where he was present with a weapon.
A witness’s trial testimony described his participation in the incident.
The investigating agency excluded him from the charge-sheet after an application by his father and submitted a report making findings about his innocence and presence.
The Court found the submission that he should have been included in the charge-sheet well-founded and stated that the application to add him deserved to be allowed prima facie.
issues.conclusion: The Court concluded that the record prima facie supported adding the person as an accused, but referred the governing questions about the timing and threshold for exercising the power to a three-judge Bench and did not finally dispose of the application in this judgment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 319(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure allows a court, during an inquiry or trial, to proceed against a person not already accused when the evidence indicates that the person committed an offence triable with the existing accused. Section 173 requires an investigating officer to report the investigation rather than make judicial findings. Y. Saraba Reddy v. Puthur Rami Reddy held that an investigating officer’s satisfaction is not determinative of the court’s assessment under Section 319. The Court also relied on the principles in Joginder Singh v. State of Punjab and Michael Machado v. Central Bureau of Investigation, while referring the applicable threshold for further consideration.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_refusal_to_add_accused and person_named_in_initial_report and person_arrested_at_scene and trial_testimony_implicates_person and investigative_report_excludes_person

predicates.appeal_challenges_refusal_to_add_accused: An appeal challenges a lower court’s refusal to add a person as an accused during a criminal trial.
predicates.person_named_in_initial_report: The person is identified as involved in the initial report of the alleged offence.
predicates.person_arrested_at_scene: Police arrest the person at the scene of the alleged offence.
predicates.trial_testimony_implicates_person: A witness’s testimony during trial describes the person as participating in the alleged offence.
predicates.investigative_report_excludes_person: The investigating agency’s report excludes the person from those sent for trial.

issues.definition: When a person sought to be added was named in the initial report, arrested at the scene, implicated by trial testimony, and excluded by the investigative report, the record may prima facie support adding that person as an accused.
